# Zammy

> Zammy reads news from several upstream providers, joins the same story as different
> outlets ran it, and shows each story as a timeline of the days it was covered. It links
> to the original articles and does not host their text.

**Fetch the JSON, not the HTML.** Every page except a storyline's own is a JavaScript
application whose served markup is an empty shell — `https://www.zammy.info/` and any
`?q=` search will look blank to anything that does not execute scripts. Two things are
readable without JavaScript: the JSON under `/api/v1/` below, and the server-rendered
storyline pages at `/storyline/<uuid>/<slug>`. The JSON is the better source; the pages
exist so the same content is reachable by something that only reads HTML.

**The words below are used precisely**, and reading them loosely will misread a response:

- **Sighting** — one emission of an article by an upstream provider. Providers re-emit the
  same story under fresh identifiers, so a sighting is an observation, not a story.
  `sightingCount` on an article counts these, and it measures upstream's chattiness rather
  than the story's importance. Do not rank by it.
- **Article** — one real-world news story, identified by its canonical URL. This is the
  unit with a headline, a source and a publication time.
- **Group** — one story as several outlets ran it: the same piece syndicated at different
  URLs, kept as separate articles and joined. Most groups hold one article.
- **Storyline** — one specific event or evolving situation ("Canada EU Partnership", never
  bare "Canada"), as a persistent collection of groups identified by a UUID and unbounded
  in time. This is the unit worth citing.
- **Day** — a storyline is paged by day. Each day it has coverage carries that day's
  articles and, usually, a one-sentence summary written for it.

**Storyline UUIDs are stable and safe to keep.** Storylines merge, and a merge keeps the
absorbed UUID as an alias: an old id resolves to the survivor rather than breaking, and
`/storyline/<old-uuid>/…` answers `301` to the survivor's URL. An id you stored last month
still means something today.

**What Zammy does not have:** article body text, paywalled content, or any writing of its
own about the news beyond the day summaries. Headlines and links belong to the outlets that
published them and should be attributed and linked to those outlets, not to Zammy.

**Rate limiting** applies to `/api/` only, per IP, and every response carries
`x-ratelimit-limit` / `x-ratelimit-remaining` — read those rather than assuming a number.
The static files and the storyline pages are not limited. `/api/v1/trending` and the
storyline pages are cached at the edge, so repeated identical requests are cheap; a wide
fan-out of distinct `/api/v1/timeline` queries is not, and each new keyword search spends
upstream provider quota.

## API

- [Trending storylines](https://www.zammy.info/api/v1/trending): the storylines a rolling
  window found several newsrooms covering, busiest and freshest first. Each carries `id`,
  `label`, `size`, `sourceCount` and `lastUpdated`. Optional `language` (default `en`) and
  `limit` (1–100, default 60). The best starting point, and the cheapest.
- [Timeline](https://www.zammy.info/api/v1/timeline?q=climate): a keyword search as a
  time-ordered timeline. Takes `q` (required unless `storyline` is given), `language`,
  `country`, `from`/`to` (ISO 8601), `limit` (1–100, default 25) and an opaque `cursor`
  for paging. Returns `items` — one slot per storyline-day, each with its lead article,
  syndicated copies and the rest of that day's coverage.
- [One storyline's coverage](https://www.zammy.info/api/v1/timeline?storyline=b3fd657c-e75d-4e58-81c2-18d724523715):
  the same endpoint with `storyline=<uuid>` and no `q` — one storyline's whole arc, which
  is what the storyline pages are built from.
- [Reference values](https://www.zammy.info/api/v1/reference): the language and country
  codes `language` and `country` accept, as name → code maps. Fetch once; it rarely
  changes.
- [Topic detail](https://www.zammy.info/api/v1/topics/): append a 64-character hex
  fingerprint from a timeline response's `topic.fingerprint` to see what has been fetched
  for that search and over what span.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.zammy.info/): the search box and a cloud of current storylines.
  Requires JavaScript.
- [Sitemap](https://www.zammy.info/sitemap.xml): every storyline page currently worth
  crawling, with `lastmod`. Generated per request from the same query that feeds
  `/api/v1/trending`, so it lists what is live now rather than an ever-growing archive.
- [A storyline page](https://www.zammy.info/storyline/b3fd657c-e75d-4e58-81c2-18d724523715/canada-eu-partnership):
  `/storyline/<uuid>/<slug>`, server-rendered. The slug is cosmetic — only the UUID is
  read, so a stale slug still resolves. Each day appears with its summary and that day's
  headlines as outbound links.

## Optional

- [Crawler policy](https://www.zammy.info/robots.txt): agents that fetch because a reader
  asked, and agents that index so Zammy can be found, are welcome. Crawlers collecting
  training corpora are not.
